carriers.name: Google Fi Wireless
carriers.description: Owned by Google. Switches automatically between the different listed host networks and Wi-Fi hotspots based on factors such as relative signal strength.
carriers.family_discounts: Per-line price drops with group size up to 6 lines (e.g. Unlimited Premium $65 for 1 line to $40/line at 4-6 lines; Standard $50 to $25/line; Essentials $35 to ~$22.50/line; Flexible $20 + $15 per additional line, plus data). All members of a group must be on the same plan; data thresholds are per person.
carriers.smartwatch_notes: Smartwatch connectivity included free on all plans (no extra line). Supported: Google Pixel Watch LTE and Samsung Galaxy Watch LTE models. Apple Watch cellular not supported.
carriers.roaming_notes: Canada/Mexico included on Unlimited Standard, Unlimited Premium and Flexible (not Essentials). Unlimited Premium includes 50GB high-speed data in 200+ destinations then 256 kbps; Flexible charges the same $10/GB abroad; Standard/Essentials have no data outside CA/MX. No day passes. Cellular calls abroad ~20 cents/min; texts free abroad on Premium/Flexible.

networks.priority: Fi advertises "top-priority data speeds"
networks.notes: Fi uses T-Mobile as its US host network; mid-band 5G (Ultra Capacity) access on supported phones per common knowledge, not stated explicitly on the plans page.

plans.name: Unlimited Premium
plans.line_pricing_notes: Totals from fi.google.com/about/plans: 1-6 lines $65/$110/$135/$160/$200/$240. Everyone in a group must be on the same plan. Promo: 50% off for 12 months when bringing a Pixel (ends 10/31/26). Taxes & gov't fees extra; no autopay requirement.
plans.throttle_speed_after: 256 kbps after 100GB (or $10/GB to restore)
plans.international: Free calls from the US to 50+ destinations (incl. Canada & Mexico); unlimited texts from US to other countries; other destinations at per-minute rates.
perks: 50% off for 12 months when bringing a Pixel phone (promo, ends 10/31/26)
plans.watch_notes: All Fi plans include full connectivity (calls, texts, data) for select smartwatches at no extra cost, without adding a line. Fi watch page lists Google Pixel Watch 3/4/5 LTE and Samsung Galaxy Watch8/Watch9/Watch Ultra models; no Apple Watch listed (Apple Watch cellular not supported). Watch data counts toward the plan high-speed allowance.
plans.roam_cm_notes: Included; counts toward 50GB high-speed international allowance, then 256 kbps · Canada/Mexico are among the 200+ covered destinations.
plans.roam_global_notes: 50GB high-speed data in 200+ destinations (5G in 110+), then 256 kbps. Texts free abroad; cellular calls abroad ~20 cents/min; Wi-Fi calls to US/CA/MX free. No travel passes needed. International data suspended if majority of usage is abroad over 90 days.

carriers.roaming_notes: AiR publishes no roaming terms. International calling (Agent +) and Canada/Mexico calling plus international texting (Super Agent plans) are included, but roaming in Canada, Mexico or elsewhere is not described.
carriers.status_notes: Rebranded as 'AiR' (AiR by Lexvor / Air Lexvor Inc.), an AI-agent-focused phone service. lexvor.com permanently redirects (308) to useair.net.

networks.priority: Standard (reseller) priority, below the host network's own premium traffic during congestion (per AiR Network Management page)
networks.notes: AiR's public pages say only 'a major nationwide 5G host network'. The official phone-compatibility checker (useair.net/shop/check-imei, backed by /shop/api/device/check) answers an unknown IMEI with "We couldn't find this IMEI in T-Mobile's device database". That indicates the service uses T-Mobile's device database, so T-Mobile is the host (medium confidence; the network is still not named in marketing copy). Older 2024 forum claims of Verizon predate the AiR relaunch. Ultra Capacity access is unknown.

carriers.name: Metro by T-Mobile
carriers.description: Owned by T-Mobile. Formerly MetroPCS.
carriers.family_discounts: Multi-line totals come from each plan's Broadband Facts label (before AutoPay). The $40 Period, $50 and $55 plans have volume pricing: $40 plan 1-4 lines $40/$65/$90/$100; $50 plan $55/$85/$115/$125; $55 plan $60/$95/$130/$140. Each label lists up to 4 lines. The BYOD web plans ($25/$30/$35) are priced flat per line (no discount) for up to 5 lines. AutoPay saves $5 on a single line, and its multi-line effect is not published.
carriers.smartwatch_notes: Watch lines are $10/mo (unlimited data, talk & text, picture messaging) for Apple Watch and Samsung watches. They drop to $5/mo with your own device on the $55 AutoPay plan (in store). Metro is on Apple's US Apple Watch carrier list.
carriers.roaming_notes: The $35 BYOD plan includes Mexico/Canada unlimited calls/texts and 5GB roaming data. Other $40+ plans can add Mexico & Canada Unlimited for $5/mo (5GB) or $10/mo (10GB). Roaming elsewhere goes through partner carriers in select countries, and no included allowance or day pass was found.
carriers.status_notes: T-Mobile-owned prepaid brand.

networks.priority: Deprioritized vs T-Mobile postpaid on most plans (slower after 35GB/50GB when busy); $55 plan advertises 'unlimited premium 5G data that won't slow you down'

carriers.name: Spectrum Mobile
carriers.description: Owned by Charter Communications. Tablet and wearable plans available. T-Mobile network available to business customers only.
carriers.family_discounts: No volume discount on Unlimited ($30/line) or Unlimited Plus ($40/line) - same per-line price at any line count. Unlimited Plus Premium is $60 for a single line or $50/line with 2+ lines. Plans can be mixed per line. Up to 20 lines (third-party). Promos: one Unlimited line free for 12 months (or Plus first line $10/mo, Premium first line $20/mo) for new customers with Spectrum Internet; $20 activation per line; +$10/line/mo if Spectrum Internet is not maintained.
carriers.smartwatch_notes: Smartwatch Access is $10/mo per watch (unlimited data on LTE/5G plus talk/text, per third-party guides); included free for one watch on Unlimited Plus Premium. Cellular Apple Watch (Series 3+) supported since 2021 with an iPhone on Spectrum Mobile; Family Setup not supported. Samsung Galaxy Watch support unconfirmed; Google Pixel Watch reportedly unsupported. Official spectrum.net support pages could not be read (cookie wall).
carriers.roaming_notes: Unlimited: no included roaming; Global Day Pass $5/day (Canada/Mexico) or $10/day (190+ countries) per line. Unlimited Plus: free roaming in 215+ countries, 10 GB high-speed then reduced. Unlimited Plus Premium: free roaming calls/texts plus 20 GB high-speed in 215+ countries incl. Canada & Mexico. Global Pass Extra ($5/$10 per day) adds high-speed data. Throttled speeds and exact country lists not published in sources read. All plans: 2,000 min/mo calling US to Canada & Mexico.
carriers.status_notes: Requires an active Spectrum Internet (residential) subscription; per WhistleOut and Spectrum-page search snippets, if Spectrum Internet is not maintained an extra $10/line/mo applies to Unlimited and Unlimited Plus and additional lines cannot be added. Charter-owned cable MVNO. WhistleOut notes Cox Mobile merged into Spectrum Mobile on 2026-09-16 (existing Cox customers keep plans/devices). By the Gig plans no longer sold to new customers as of July 2026 (Light Reading / The Desk).

networks.notes: Verizon MVNO (Charter newsroom / Light Reading 2026-07-22), plus ~45 million Spectrum WiFi access points with 'Speed Boost' and Charter CBRS offload in some areas. Spectrum's 5G resources page says only that its 5G 'combines low-band and high-band coverage'; no source read confirms or denies Verizon 5G Ultra Wideband (C-band) access, so premium_5g stays null.

plans.name: Unlimited
plans.line_pricing_notes: Flat $30/line at any line count per Charter/Light Reading (2026-07-22), The Desk, WhistleOut and HighSpeedInternet. Plans can be mixed per line. A Spectrum-page search snippet mentioning a '$40/mo standard price for one Unlimited line' could not be read in context (spectrum.com timed out) and conflicts with every other source; older (2022-era) $45 single-line pricing is outdated. Max 20 lines per WhistleOut/HighSpeedInternet (UpPhone says 12). +$10/line/mo without Spectrum Internet.
plans.throttle_speed_after: Reduced speeds during congestion after 30 GB
plans.international: 2,000 min/mo from US to Canada & Mexico included; international texting from the US included; other international calling rates not confirmed.
perks: Promo: one Unlimited line free for 12 months (bill credits) for new customers with Spectrum Internet + AutoPay
plans.watch_notes: Smartwatch Access $10/mo per watch (Charter press release values it at $10/mo; HighSpeedInternet). Apple Watch Series 3+ supported with an iPhone on Spectrum Mobile; Family Setup not supported. Samsung Galaxy Watch support reported only by an undated community answer; Pixel Watch reportedly not supported.

carriers.name: Straight Talk
carriers.description: Owned by Verizon. Tablet plans available. Rooted or jailbroken devices not allowed.
carriers.family_discounts: Family Plan of 2-5 lines on the unlimited tiers. Savings off the sum of individual prices: $15/mo with 2 lines, $45 with 3, $80 with 4, $100 with 5. Silver per line: $45/$37.50/$30/$25/$25; Gold: $55/$47.50/$40/$35/$35; Platinum: $65/$57.50/$50/$45/$45. Family Plan doesn't combine with the Auto Pay discount, which is a 3-month single-line promo ($1 Bronze, $2.50 Silver, $5 Gold/Platinum). StraightSAVINGS! and Tablet plans are excluded from multi-line discounts. Bronze shows no family discount.
carriers.smartwatch_notes: Straight Talk sells no cellular smartwatch plans and is not on Apple's Apple Watch cellular carrier list. A GPS watch paired to a Straight Talk phone works over Bluetooth only. Tablet Unlimited lines are offered instead ($10/mo with Silver or Gold, included with Platinum).
carriers.roaming_notes: Gold and Platinum include Canada & Mexico roaming (unlimited text, 300 min talk, 10 GB data). Other plans and other countries need the 7-Day International Roaming perk: 5 GB data, 300 min, unlimited messaging, up to 5 per line per cycle, primary use must be in the US. Its price isn't rendered on the official page; third parties list $20. International calling perks require calls to originate in the US/Puerto Rico.

networks.notes: Silver, Gold and Platinum Unlimited include Verizon 5G Ultra Wideband (Verizon press release 2026-10-19; FCC Broadband Facts labels on straighttalk.com list 5G Ultra Wideband typical speeds 163-622 Mbps down for all three). Bronze 10 GB label lists only 5G / 4G LTE (no UW). StraightSAVINGS! reportedly 5G but not 5G UW (third-party). Unlimited plans carry the disclaimer 'speeds may temporarily reduce in times of congestion'; exact QCI/priority not published. Site still shows legacy LTE-only terms for customers 'not on the Verizon network' (legacy lines); new activations are on Verizon.

A third-party Lifeline review (freegovernmentiphones.org, verified 2026-08-10) says 'primarily on AT&T, with T-Mobile in some markets'. That T-Mobile claim is unconfirmed, so host_networks stays [att].

carriers.name: TDS Mobile
carriers.description: Owned by TDS Telecom.
carriers.family_discounts: No multi-line discount at standard rates: up to 6 lines per residential account (25 on business), each priced per line, Unlimited and By the Gig can be mixed. Current promo takes 50% off each new line for 12 months for TDS Internet customers (lost if internet is cancelled).
carriers.smartwatch_notes: Not supported. TDS Mobile is phones-only; plans are not available for smartwatches or tablets.
carriers.roaming_notes: Domestic off-network roaming permitted (max 50% of monthly usage per line, may be slowed to 2G). No included Canada/Mexico or international roaming; international roaming and calling are prepaid add-ons whose rates are shown only at purchase and are excluded from promos and the money-back guarantee.
carriers.status_notes: Requires TDS broadband internet service (not available in California). Launched 2025 by TDS Telecom via NCTC/Reach agreements; unrelated to the former UScellular wireless business (sold to T-Mobile in 2025). Phones only: smartwatches and tablets are not supported.

networks.notes: Light Reading (2025-11-19) reports the service is built on NCTC's agreements with Reach and AT&T, and the TDS coverage-map page embeds AT&T's reseller map (att.com/idpmaps/reseller). TDS's own policies call the host only an unnamed 'Network Provider'/'licensed national wireless carrier'. Network management policy lists typical 5G speeds of 35-158 Mbps down / 3-21 Mbps up (LTE 11-64 / 1-10). 5G+ access not stated. Priority not disclosed; the provider may assign priority dynamically. Domestic off-network roaming capped at 50% of monthly usage per line.

plans.name: Unlimited
plans.line_pricing_notes: Each line individually priced at the standard rate; no volume discount. Current promo: 50% off each new line for 12 months (about $15/line) while TDS Internet stays active; launch promo was 'Buy one line, get one 50% off'. Prices exclude taxes, SIM kit/connection fees and surcharges.
plans.throttle_speed_after: Max 512 kbps for rest of billing cycle after 30 GB high-speed per line (hotspot counts toward the 30 GB)
plans.international: Not included; international calling is a prepaid add-on with unpublished rates (excluded from plan price and promo).
perks: Up to 6 lines, priced per line
50% off new lines for 12 months when bundled with TDS Internet (promo; $15/line)
plans.watch_notes: TDS says plans are not available for smartwatches or tablets ('Currently, TDS Mobile supports phones only').
plans.roam_cm_notes: Not included; only via prepaid international roaming add-on · Service terms: international roaming and calling plans are only available as add-on prepaid services; rates not published on any readable page. Promo discounts do not apply to data roaming fees.
plans.roam_global_notes: Prepaid add-on only; prices, countries and terms shown at purchase (mobile.tdstelecom.com/international-calling-services returned HTTP 405).

plans.name: By the Gig
plans.line_pricing_notes: Each line individually priced (base price includes 1 GB); extra data billed per line at $5/GB. Promo 50% off new lines for 12 months.
plans.throttle_speed_after: Extra GB auto-added at $5 each (up to 5 more GB / $25, billed in whole GB); after 6 GB total, max 512 kbps for rest of cycle
plans.international: Not included; prepaid add-on with unpublished rates.
perks: Mix and match with Unlimited lines
plans.watch_notes: Phones only; smartwatches and tablets not supported.
plans.roam_cm_notes: Not included; only via prepaid international roaming add-on · Add-on rates not published on readable pages.
plans.roam_global_notes: Prepaid add-on only; rates not published on readable pages.

carriers.name: Tello Mobile
carriers.description: Owned by KeepCalling. Tello originally used the Sprint network, but transitioned to using the T-Mobile network after the T-Mobile and Sprint merger.
carriers.family_discounts: No multi-line discount. Multiple lines can be managed under one Tello account with no extra per-line fee (Tello Family), but each line keeps its own plan and price and nothing is shared. Max lines per account not published.
carriers.smartwatch_notes: No paired/number-share watch plans. Standalone eSIM Android watches (e.g. Samsung Galaxy Watch LTE) can reportedly use a separate Tello line on any plan; Apple Watch is not supported (Tello help center via search snippet). Sources conflict (BestPhonePlans: not supported).
carriers.roaming_notes: No roaming included by default. International roaming (200+ countries, incl. Canada/Mexico) is pay-per-use from Pay As You Go credit after activation (min $5 balance); Tello's May 2025 rates: 5c/min, 1c/SMS, 1c/MB in most destinations. Limited-time free roaming in 54 European countries using normal plan allowances through 2027-01-31 (Tello blog 2026-09-29; an older tello.com snippet said 2026-09-30, so verify). Wi-Fi calling works abroad. Calls from the US to 60+ countries including Canada and Mexico are free from plan minutes.

networks.priority: Deprioritized behind T-Mobile postpaid and some prepaid (Reviews.org)
networks.notes: WhistleOut lists 'T-Mobile 5G Network in select areas'; Tello blog says plans run on 'America's largest 5G network'. 5G Ultra Capacity access not confirmed. Third-party listings report video at 480p (SD).

plans.name: 300 Minutes + 2GB
plans.line_pricing_notes: Multiple lines can be held on one Tello account (no extra per-line fee), but each line is individually priced and data/balances are not shared; no multi-line discount. Maximum lines per account not published.
plans.throttle_speed_after: Data stops at cap; top-ups available
plans.international: Free calling to 60+ countries (incl. Canada & Mexico) from plan minutes; other destinations billed from PAYG credit
perks: Hotspot can use all plan data
plans.watch_notes: A cellular watch needs its own standalone Tello line/plan (no number sharing). Tello help center (via search snippet) says Apple Watch does not work with Tello eSIM but eSIM smartwatches such as Samsung do. $6 = cheapest data plan (no minutes + 2GB, per PhoneArena grid) and matches BestMVNO's '$6/mo smartwatch add-on'. carriers.family_discounts: No multi-line or family discount found. Up to 10 lines can be activated under one account (same email), each bought as its own plan at the regular single-line price.
carriers.smartwatch_notes: No smartwatch support found. Unreal sells phone (talk/text/data) SIMs for smartphones only; the help center says SIMs don't work in hotspot/internet devices and use in unintended devices isn't supported.
carriers.roaming_notes: Roaming in Canada & Mexico is included on all plans: unlimited talk/text plus 1GB high-speed data (Mini, Midi) or 5GB (Maxi). Top-ups: 1GB $20, 2GB $30, 5GB $50. No other international roaming is documented officially.
carriers.status_notes: Red Pocket-owned prepaid brand. New plan lineup (Mini/Midi/Maxi with 10/25/50GB) replaced legacy plans; activations before Dec 2025 may keep legacy plans.

networks.priority: MVNO / deprioritized during congestion (third-party)
networks.notes: Official help center: current plans run on the 'GSMA' network (Red Pocket's name for AT&T); APN settings use MCC 310 / MNC 410 (AT&T), MMSC mmsc.mobile.att.net, APN ERESELLER / unreal.com.attz; GSMA device list links to an AT&T PDF. Plans were on 'GSMT' (T-Mobile) before May 2023 (legacy only). 5G+ unconfirmed: PhoneCompass cites FCC-label typical '5G+' speeds (152-472 Mbps) but the official labels could not be read.

carriers.description: Owned by Ahmed Khattak. Unlimited plans with discounts and Perks with 3 or more lines.
carriers.family_discounts: No multi-line discount on Unlimited Premium/Starter/Flex: each line is the 1-line price. 3+ monthly Unlimited Premium lines earn one subscription perk (up to $15/mo value). By the Gig/Light 2GB are shared pools: pool price includes 1 line, +$8/mo per added line, no stated line limit. Multi-Network add-on $10/mo per line ($7.50/mo annual).
carriers.smartwatch_notes: Watch plans $6.50/mo or $78/yr (taxes incl.), Warp (Verizon) network only. Apple Watch: companion and standalone (standalone needs iPhone for setup); Pixel Watch 2+: companion only; Samsung: only Galaxy Watch9 and Watch Ultra2, companion with Android phone. Companion plan free with Unlimited Premium on Warp (or Premium + Multi-Network add-on on Warp). 5G watches currently LTE-only.
carriers.roaming_notes: Included roaming: Unlimited Premium 20GB + 200 min + 250 texts/month; Annual Unlimited Starter 1GB + 200 min + 250 texts. Others buy packs ($15: 1GB/150 min/150 texts; $30: 5GB/500/500). Country counts by network: Light Speed 180+, Warp 125+, Dark Star 110+ (30 data-only). carriers.description: Owned by Verizon. Operates on Verizon's native 4G/LTE network and WiFi calling (no 3G – Verizon will shut this down at the end of 2020 anyway or roaming- some reports of LTEiRA roaming with talk and text). No toll-free customer service #; service provided via in-app chat, text, Facebook, or Twitter; callbacks by request. Visible Connect assists nonprofit technology startups. With party pay it's exactly $25 a month taxes&fees included.
carriers.family_discounts: Visible has no family/multi-line plan; each line is a separate account with its own payment. 'Inner Circle' lets up to 7 Visible members link accounts; with 2+ members, Visible+ and Visible+ Pro monthly members each save $5/mo (no stacking with other service promos like 5OFF5). Base Visible plan gets no multi-line discount.
carriers.smartwatch_notes: Cellular smartwatches supported: Apple Watch (Series 4+, needs iPhone on Visible) and select Android watches (Pixel Watch LTE, Galaxy Watch 8/8 Classic/Ultra per 2025 reports). $10/mo on Visible and Visible+; included free with Visible+ Pro. Watch shares the phone's number.
carriers.roaming_notes: Global Pass: $5/day for Canada, Mexico, Puerto Rico & USVI (base Visible plan only - included on Visible+/Pro), $10/day in 140+ other countries; unlimited talk/text/data with 2GB/day high-speed then 3G. Visible+ includes 1 free Global Pass day/mo (12/yr on annual), Visible+ Pro 2/mo (24/yr annual), bankable. Visible+/Pro include Mexico/Canada roaming with 2GB/day high-speed. Domestic roaming included (may be 2G speeds).

isps.name: altafiber
isps.pricing_basis: Promo prices are advertised 'starting at' prices with the eBill discount (about $5/mo), from myutilitysearch.com (updated 2026-10-25), cross-checked against altafiber.com search snippets. altafiber.com pages fetched today render plan prices only via JS (price fields blank). From the official pages: 'Prices starting at just $30/mo', promo terms (1 Gig and 2 Gig 2 years; 3 Gig and 6 Gig 3 years), free activation online, and Fioptics Home at $20/mo (free with 3 Gig). Regular post-promo prices are mostly unknown.
isps.status_notes: altafiber is the consumer brand of Cincinnati Bell Inc., which has been owned by Macquarie Asset Management since 2021. It sells Fioptics fiber in Greater Cincinnati, Dayton, Northern Kentucky and SE Indiana. Hawaiian Telcom is a Cincinnati Bell subsidiary. Its site uses the altafiber logo, but its header and copyright still say 'Hawaiian Telcom' and it has its own plans and prices. Hawaii is therefore NOT included in this file; see research_notes.

plans.notes: Matches altafiber's 'starting at $30/mo' claim. altafiber also advertises Internet + TV at $30 each per month when bundled, and its order link references a 100Mbps package. Equipment: Fioptics Home (gateway + 1 extender + Fioptics Care + tech support) is $20/mo. Without it, gateway rental is reported as $15/mo (myutilitysearch), $11.99 (altafiber holiday page snippet) or $9.99 (a review), so the fee is unclear.

plans.name: Fioptics 600
plans.notes: myutilitysearch gives $40 for 12 months. internetproviders.ai (May 2026) lists $44.99. ISP Reports (FCC-label data, Jan 2026) lists $50. myutilitysearch says regular rates typically run $15-$20 above promo. A 400 Mbps tier ($40) is also listed by myutilitysearch only.

All prices include a $10/mo autopay + e-bill (ACH) discount. Post-promo regular rates are not published (HighSpeedInternet: roughly +$20/mo in year two), so price_monthly is null for 12-month promos. Astound is still sold under its own brand.

isps.status_notes: AT&T completed its $5.75B all-cash acquisition of Lumen's mass-markets (consumer) fiber business on Feb 2, 2026 (about 1M fiber subscribers and 4M+ fiber locations, incl. Denver, Seattle, Salt Lake City, Las Vegas, Portland, Minneapolis-St. Paul); former Lumen/CenturyLink/Quantum Fiber customers are being converted to the AT&T Fiber brand (Quantum Fiber has its own file). On Jun 7, 2026 AT&T cut its fiber lineup from six tiers to four (300 Mbps, 500 Mbps, 1 GIG, 5 GIG), dropping 100 Mbps and 2 GIG. AT&T plans to exit its copper network in most of its wireline footprint by end of 2029.

plans.notes: $89.99 w/ Autopay & paperless ($99.99 without). Select areas only.

plans.name: Fiber 8 Gig
plans.notes: $119.99 w/ Autopay & paperless ($129.99 without). $250 prepaid Mastercard for new customers. Select areas only.

isps.name: Cox
isps.pricing_basis: No Cox-branded plans are sold to new customers; former Cox markets are sold Spectrum plans at Spectrum pricing (see spectrum.json).
isps.status_notes: Charter Communications completed its $34.5B acquisition of Cox Communications on Aug 20, 2026. Spectrum products, pricing and packaging rolled out to former Cox markets from mid-September 2026, and the Spectrum brand is used in all markets. cox.com now presents as 'Cox is now Spectrum' and cox.com/residential/internet.html is titled 'Spectrum Internet Plans | Fiber-Powered Speeds from $30/mo.' Existing legacy Cox customers keep their current products and prices unless they choose to change. New customers in former Cox areas buy Spectrum plans (see spectrum.json). Within a year of closing, Charter's parent company is to rename itself Cox Communications while keeping the Spectrum consumer brand.

isps.name: EarthLink
isps.pricing_basis: Plan prices excluding the $14.95/mo modem/gateway lease and taxes. These are from WhistleOut's EarthLink listings (checked 2026-10-27), because earthlink.net shows no prices without an address except the 5G page's 'Plans starting at $59.95/mo.' EarthLink advertises a 12-month rate lock ('No change in what you pay for 12 months').
isps.status_notes: Mostly a reseller. EarthLink, LLC sells fiber, 5G home (wireless) and satellite internet over partner networks rather than its own last-mile plant. It markets itself as 'the largest internet service provider in the country' and says it covers '96% of the U.S.', claims that only make sense across partner footprints. Its 5G service is a cellular-data resale (a reviewer's speed test showed T-Mobile). Its satellite service is a GEO resale (EarthLink says 'up to 100 Mbps' and 'geostationary'), with the underlying operator not named. A CEO interview (Fierce, seen only as a search snippet) says the fiber rides the networks of four major telecom partners, also unnamed. Which plan you get depends on the partner network at the address.

plans.name: Fiber 100 Mbps
plans.notes: 'Available in select locations' (WhistleOut). WhistleOut lists 100/10 Mbps, but EarthLink's fiber page advertises 'Symmetrical speeds for uploads and downloads', so upload is null. $24.95 one-time professional installation. No term contract per WhistleOut. Some third parties claim a 12-month contract and an ETF up to $200, which is unverified.

plans.name: Fiber 500 Mbps
plans.notes: WhistleOut ('HyperLink' 500): $34.95 plan + $14.95 modem 'for the first 3 months, then $54.95/month'. WhistleOut doesn't say whether $54.95 includes the modem. Its convention elsewhere (e.g. Viasat) is plan-only, so it is recorded as the plan price. The 3-month intro sits oddly with the advertised 12-month rate lock.

plans.name: Fiber 1 Gig
plans.notes: WhistleOut ('HyperLink' 1 Gbps) broadband-facts table: $44.95/mo introductory for 3 months, then $74.95/mo (modem inclusion unclear; recorded as plan price). No contract, '1-Year' price lock, $14.95/mo modem lease, $24.95 installation (no-show fee equals the install fee). WhistleOut lists upload as 20 Mbps, which conflicts with EarthLink's 'symmetrical' claim, so upload is null.

plans.name: Fiber 2 Gig
plans.notes: 'Available in select locations' (WhistleOut).

plans.name: Fiber 5 Gig
plans.notes: EarthLink's 'FASTEST' plan ('up to 5000 Mbps'). Price from WhistleOut ('Available in select locations').

plans.name: 5G Home Internet Unlimited
plans.data_cap_notes: Marketed as unlimited with 'no throttling'. WhistleOut's plan features say 800 GB of high-speed data, and EarthLink's footnote says it 'may temporarily slow data speeds... including if the network is busy.'
plans.notes: earthlink.net: 'Plans starting at $59.95/mo.' Month-to-month, no credit check, self-install with same-day shipping. Router leased, with a 'monthly router fee' as a separate line item ($14.95/mo per WhistleOut and SatelliteInternet.com). 'Some users report speeds up to 425 Mbps'; no speed guarantee. Usable only at the service address. Upfront fee is disputed: $79.95 (WhistleOut), or a $39.95 processing & handling fee or $49.99 activation (SatelliteInternet.com, Oct 20 2026). The WhistleOut figure is recorded. SatelliteInternet.com also lists $79.95/mo and $74.99/mo in places. Runs on a carrier 5G/LTE network (a reviewer's test showed T-Mobile). Measured rural latency 60-200+ ms (one reviewer), so latency is null.

isps.name: Fidium Fiber
isps.pricing_basis: Promo prices are from fidiumfiber.com/fiber-internet, read 2026-10-27. They are first-year prices for new service and require AutoPay (bank account) plus paperless billing; taxes are extra. price_monthly is the Monthly Price on Fidium's residential FCC Broadband Facts labels, read today. The labels say it is 'not an introductory rate' and 'does not include discounts', so it is a pre-discount list price. Fidium only says 'Standard rates apply after promo', and Reviews.org says the jump is about $20, so the actual month-13 bill may be below the label price.
isps.status_notes: Formerly Consolidated Communications. The company went private in Dec 2024 after its merger with Condor Holdings LLC, backed by funds of Searchlight Capital Partners and British Columbia Investment Management Corp. In Sep 2025 it rebranded the whole company as Fidium. Gaurav Juneja became CEO in early 2026. The company says about 60% of its footprint is fiber, with 70% targeted in 2026 and 80%+ by 2027. Remaining customers are on legacy copper.

plans.name: 300 Mbps (Light Use)
plans.notes: Latency is shown on the label as under 8 ms. The WiFi gateway is optional at $10/mo (bring your own allowed); it is included free only on 1 Gig and faster. Professional install ($199) is waived. Paper invoices cost $5/mo. Extenders are $5/mo (limited time) or $7/mo. Not eligible for the one-month-free offer. A 100 Mbps residential label ($75/mo, 100/100) also exists but the tier is not on the current plans page.

plans.name: 1 Gig (Busy Homes)
plans.notes: Advertised as 'as low as $50/mo' plus one month free (credited on the 1st or 2nd bill). The WiFi gateway ($10/mo value) is included in the advertised price. A separate Fidium 'doorbuster' landing page offers 1 Gig at $20/mo for the first year (limited time, no end date stated). Label price is $115 before discounts.

plans.name: 2 Gig (Power Users)
plans.notes: Includes the premium whole-home WiFi gateway and one month free. The doorbuster landing page offers 2 Gig at $30/mo for the first year (limited time). Label price is $130 before discounts.

plans.name: 5 Gig (Creators & Pros)
plans.notes: Includes a WiFi 7 gateway and one month free. Label price is $150 before discounts. Availability is limited by location.

plans.name: 8 Gig (Future Ready)
plans.notes: Includes a WiFi 7 gateway and one month free. Label price is $190 before discounts. Availability is limited by location.

isps.name: Frontier
isps.pricing_basis: Prices with Auto Pay & paperless billing, from HighSpeedInternet.com (Jul 29, 2026); Fiber 1 Gig $64.99 confirmed on frontier.com/shop/deals on 2026-10-27. frontier.com does not list prices for the other tiers without an address.
isps.status_notes: Owned by Verizon but still sold under the Frontier brand, so status is 'active' (same convention as Mint Mobile under T-Mobile). Verizon completed its ~$20B acquisition of Frontier Communications in January 2026 (Jan 20, 2026 per news coverage). The brand continues as Frontier / 'Frontier, a Verizon Company' and frontier.com still sells Frontier Fiber plans (site footer '(c) 2026 Verizon'). Frontier says its fiber plans 'will stay the same' for now but 'eventually plans will standardize across the entire Verizon territory'; billing, accounts and support are not yet combined with Verizon. No Fios rebrand announced as of 2026-10-27.

mobile_bundles.eligible_internet_plans: Residential Frontier Fiber plans of $20/mo or more after promotions and discounts
mobile_bundles.eligible_mobile_plans: Any postpaid (and per the FAQ, prepaid) Verizon mobile phone plan; excludes employee, business and data-only plans
mobile_bundles.notes: frontier.com/verizon-customer: '$15/mo discount on residential Frontier Fiber internet plans of $20/mo or more' with a Verizon mobile phone plan; enrollment required; applied in 1-2 billing cycles. The page's footnote says postpaid only while its FAQ says prepaid and postpaid Verizon Value brands also qualify (conflict). frontier.com/shop/deals: 'Save $15/mo. with Frontier Fiber and Verizon mobile.'

plans.name: Fiber 500
plans.data_cap_notes: No data caps, no overage charges (frontier.com).
plans.notes: Price per HighSpeedInternet.com (Jul 2026), w/ Auto Pay & paperless. Free Wi-Fi 7 router (frontier.com deals: Fiber 500 through 7 Gig). Install listed at $100 but usually waived (HSI). Frontier's merger page (early 2026) gave a Mobile + Home rate of $39.99 after a promo, which implies an older $54.99 base; current base appears to be $44.99.

plans.name: Fiber 1 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: No data caps, no overage charges (frontier.com).
plans.notes: frontier.com/shop/deals (2026-10-27): 'Fiber 1 Gig $64.99/mo.' with price 'guaranteed for 5-years' ('applies only to the then-current base monthly rate'), free installation ($100 value), Whole-Home Wi-Fi with Wi-Fi 7 included. Upload 1,000 Mbps max wired, location dependent (HSI). Auto Pay requirement per HSI.

plans.name: Fiber 2 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: No data caps, no overage charges (frontier.com).
plans.notes: Price per HighSpeedInternet.com (Jul 2026). Wi-Fi 7 router + Whole-Home Wi-Fi included. Current promo: free Ring Home Security Bundle ($269 value) with 2/5/7 Gig, redeem by 5/8/27. Verizon says Frontier 2 Gig+ with Verizon mobile also gets up to $10/mo mobile perk credit (search snippet).

plans.name: Fiber 5 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: No data caps, no overage charges (frontier.com).
plans.notes: Price per HighSpeedInternet.com (Jul 2026); another aggregator (MyUtilitySearch) lists ~$154.99, so treat with caution. Limited availability.

plans.name: Fiber 7 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: No data caps, no overage charges (frontier.com).
plans.notes: Price per HighSpeedInternet.com (Jul 2026). Limited availability.

isps.name: GFiber (Google Fiber)
isps.pricing_basis: Flat national list prices from gfiber.com (plans page and FAQ) read 2026-10-27; no autopay condition, no promotional pricing. Prices exclude taxes and a local access fee. GFiber says the 1 Gig price has not changed since 2012. Tier availability varies by address/building.
isps.status_notes: Google Fiber rebranded as GFiber (fiber.google.com now redirects to gfiber.com). On 2026-03-11 GFiber and Stonepeak announced GFiber will combine with Stonepeak-owned Astound Broadband into an independent provider: Stonepeak majority owner, Alphabet a significant minority shareholder, existing GFiber executive team to lead. Subject to regulatory approval; expected to close in Q4 2026 (not closed as of 2026-10-27). Webpass (building-level service in Chicago, Denver, Miami, Oakland/East Bay, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle) is still sold as 'gFiber Webpass'; webpass.net redirects to gfiber.com.

plans.name: Core 1 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: FAQ: 'gFiber does not have data caps, overage charges, or speed throttling.'
plans.notes: Wi-Fi 6E router and up to one extender included. Free self-setup or pro install. No formal price-lock term, but GFiber says this price has been the same since 2012. Equipment replacement fee if not returned within 60 days of cancelling.

plans.name: Home 3 Gig
plans.notes: Multi-gig Wi-Fi 7 router and up to two extenders included; Priority Room Optimization included; optional Internet Battery Backup and Home Phone add-ons.

plans.name: Edge 8 Gig
plans.notes: Wi-Fi 7 router with 10G port, up to two extenders, Internet Battery Backup and an Uptime Guarantee (25% refund of that month's bill if down more than 45 minutes) included.

plans.name: Webpass 1 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: None stated on the Webpass page; GFiber FAQ says no caps.
plans.notes: Apartment/condo service in select buildings in 7 metros. Month-to-month $70/mo plus taxes and fees; a yearly plan is also offered at a non-refundable $750 up front (~$62.50/mo; pages advertise 'starting at $63'). Free equipment (mesh-ready router; one extender for eligible new customers) and free pro or DIY install. Technology is not stated on the page; Webpass is historically point-to-point wireless to the building plus in-building wiring, so it is filed here as fixed_wireless. Reviews.org lists an older 500 Mbps Webpass tier ($60/mo) not shown on gfiber.com today.

isps.name: Hughesnet
isps.pricing_basis: Promo prices include a $5/mo ACH (autopay) discount, per hughesnet.com footnotes on 2026-10-27. Regular post-promo prices are from third-party reviews (SatelliteInternet.com, CNN Underscored via search summary) and equal promo plus the $25/mo 12-month discount shown on hughesnet.com. Equipment lease and taxes are extra.
isps.status_notes: Hughes Satellite Systems Corp. and 11 affiliates, including Hughes Network Systems, filed Chapter 11 on Aug 2-3 2026 in the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas, after missing about $1.5B of notes due Aug 1. EchoStar, the parent, is not a debtor. Consumer broadband subscribers fell to about 641,000 (later reported as 622,000), down about 22% year over year. Hughes says it will keep serving customers during the case and plans a multi-year shift 'from a consumer-dominated business to an enterprise and government-led platform'. Trade press expects the consumer business to wind down, but as of 2026-10-27 no shutdown or stop-sell date had been announced, and hughesnet.com was still taking new orders (promo pricing, 'Save $50 when you order online'). In a Nov 2025 SEC filing EchoStar disclosed a referral program offering Starlink to customers (per SatelliteInternet.com). Long-term viability for new subscribers is uncertain, and plans carry 12-24-month terms with ETFs.

plans.name: Lite
plans.data_cap_notes: 100 GB of Priority Data per month, then unlimited Standard Data, which 'may be slower than other traffic during high-traffic periods'. No overage fees.
plans.notes: hughesnet.com: '$39.99 per month represents a $10 per month savings for 12 months on the Lite plan,' including a $5 ACH discount kept while ACH enrollment is maintained. 'Minimum term required. Early service termination fees apply.' The post-promo price isn't stated: it could be $44.99 with ACH kept or $49.99 without, so price_monthly is null. Contract 12 months per WhistleOut's broadband-facts table. equipment_upfront = the $99 one-time lease setup fee (not a hardware purchase). Modem lease $9.99/mo. Free standard professional installation for new lease subscribers (limited time). ETF up to $400. Latency: SatelliteInternet.com says Hughesnet claims up to 650 ms on satellite-only plans.

plans.name: Select
plans.data_cap_notes: 100 GB of Priority Data per month, then unlimited (possibly slower) Standard Data.
plans.notes: hughesnet.com: 'Save $25 per month for 12 months' (not valid on Lite), then 'plans revert to the standard monthly fee'. Price Lock Guarantee: the monthly service fee won't change for 2 years, though the $25 promo still ends after 12 months. Wi-Fi 6 modem built in. The $99 lease setup fee is in equipment_upfront. Purchase option (reported $100-$449.99) available instead of lease. ETF up to $400, reduced over the term. Unreturned equipment fee up to $300.

plans.name: Elite
plans.data_cap_notes: 200 GB of Priority Data per month, then unlimited (possibly slower) Standard Data.
plans.notes: $25/mo off for 12 months on hughesnet.com; $89.99 regular per CNN Underscored (search summary) and implied by SatelliteInternet.com. Lease $14.99/mo, $99 lease setup fee, ETF up to $400.

plans.name: Fusion
plans.data_cap_notes: 200 GB of Priority Data per month, then unlimited (possibly slower) Standard Data.
plans.notes: A hybrid of GEO satellite and a terrestrial wireless link that cuts latency. 'Available only in select areas'. Technology recorded as satellite_geo because the schema has no hybrid value. Latency of about 100 ms is Hughesnet's claim per SatelliteInternet.com, and users report it is 'far from perfect'. Lease $19.99/mo, $99 lease setup fee, unreturned-equipment fee up to $500. $119.99 regular per CNN Underscored (search summary).

isps.name: Kinetic by Windstream
isps.pricing_basis: Prices include the $5/mo AutoPay credit. 'Everyday' prices and guarantee periods come from gokinetic.com/residential/offer-conditions (read 2026-10-27); the plan grid itself is only shown per address, so tier prices/promos were filled from HighSpeedInternet.com (Aug 21 2026) and MyUtilitySearch (Oct 25 2026) where they agree with the official offer terms. All offers are 'in select markets'; prices vary by address.
isps.status_notes: Windstream merged with Uniti Group in 2025 (closed Aug 2025); the combined company is Uniti Group Inc. and keeps 'Kinetic' as its consumer broadband brand. windstream.com consumer pages now redirect to gokinetic.com. Kinetic markets 'Kinetic Fiber' (300 Mbps-2 Gig; some 100 Mbps fiber) and still sells DSL on its copper footprint.

mobile_bundles.eligible_internet_plans: All Kinetic broadband plans except 100 Mbps fiber
mobile_bundles.eligible_mobile_plans: Any new or existing AT&T postpaid wireless plan (prepaid excluded)
mobile_bundles.notes: Offer conditions: '$20.00/mo. credit' on the Kinetic bill, 'for up to 24 months' while both services are kept; new Kinetic customers must activate AT&T wireless within 90 days; 'Services billed separately'; terms may change without notice.

plans.name: Fiber 100
plans.data_cap_notes: 'No annual contracts to sign or data limits.'
plans.notes: Offer conditions: '$24.99/mo with AutoPay' everyday price is based on 100Mbps service with a 1-yr guarantee; a '$19.99/mo with AutoPay' headline offer also exists 'in select markets' (duration not stated; HighSpeedInternet says 12 months). Not eligible for the AT&T Wireless credit. Gateway: Kinetic's standard Wi-Fi gateway rate is $10.99/mo unless the plan includes it or you use your own router (which tiers include it is not stated). Free professional install / $0 activation on online orders. Upload symmetrical per third-party sources.

plans.name: Fiber 300
plans.notes: Offer conditions: 'Everyday price is based on 300Mbps service (and includes $5/mo. AutoPay bill credit)' = $39.99, guarantee period 1 yr; 'Discount Offer' takes $5/mo off 300 Mbps for up to 1 year ($34.99, matching HighSpeedInternet), then 'the full amount of the then standard rate'. After the guarantee, rates 'subject to change at any time'. Gateway $10.99/mo unless included/BYO. $4/mo paper-bill fee.

plans.name: Fiber 1 Gig
plans.notes: Official 'Discount Offer': $10/mo off 1 Gig for up to 1 year; 1-yr guarantee period for 1Gig Fiber. Everyday price $49.99 is third-party (MyUtilitySearch 'verified' section, satelliteinternet/WhistleOut) and consistent with the $39.99 promo (HighSpeedInternet). HighSpeedInternet's disclaimers mention a 24-month promo in places. Gateway fee may be waived if included in plan (unconfirmed); WhistleOut says 1 Gig includes up to two extenders. Prepaid Mastercard reward (up to $200) varies by plan.

plans.name: Fiber 2 Gig
plans.notes: Official: 'Guarantee Period of 2yrs for Fiber 2 Gig service'; 'Discount Offer' $10/mo off 2 Gig for up to 2 years. $69.99 everyday price is third-party (MyUtilitySearch verified section; satelliteinternet infers Max is $20 more), $59.99 promo per HighSpeedInternet. Whether the gateway is included is not stated.

plans.name: Fiber Max 2 Gig
plans.notes: Official offer conditions: '$89.99/mo Fiber Max' with '3-year price guarantee' including the $5 AutoPay credit; return equipment or $100 fee. eero Pro 7 (Wi-Fi 7) gateway, mesh extenders as needed and Kinetic Secure Plus included (HighSpeedInternet, satelliteinternet). HighSpeedInternet and MyUtilitySearch list a $79.99 price (36 mos) - not confirmed on Kinetic's offer page, so not recorded. Upload not stated.

plans.name: DSL Internet
plans.notes: Official: 'DSL Internet for $44.99/month for 1 year with AutoPay' - line item $49.99 minus $5 AutoPay credit; $55/mo without AutoPay; 'Customer will receive highest bandwidth DSL service that Kinetic can then provide at the address'; after one year 'charged at the then current DSL rate' (not published, so price_monthly null); 'Equipment fees apply'. download_mbps 50 is HighSpeedInternet's plan label; other sources say 25-100 Mbps depending on address. Self-install-eligible copper customers choosing pro install pay $100.

isps.name: Mediacom (Xtream Internet)
isps.pricing_basis: Promo prices are the national 'starting at' offers shown on mediacomcable.com and xtream.com on 2026-10-27. They include a $10/mo autopay + paperless discount, are for new subscribers only, and exclude taxes, a $75 installation fee and a $25 activation fee. Post-promo prices are the 2026 standard rates reported by HighSpeedInternet.com (Aug 14 2026). Mediacom publishes its standard rates per market on rate cards, which could not be read.
isps.status_notes: Mediacom Communications is privately held. It sells residential internet under the Mediacom name. The xtream.com site and older marketing use the 'Xtream' brand.

mobile_bundles.eligible_internet_plans: All Mediacom Internet plans (no exclusions stated)
mobile_bundles.eligible_mobile_plans: Each Unlimited Mobile line (Unlimited $30, Unlimited Plus $40, Unlimited Ultra $60 per line)

At least one line must be transferred to Mediacom, and each line has a $10 activation fee. The mobile service is sold as 'Mediacom Mobile' (Verizon MVNO). It needs a Mediacom Internet, Home Phone or TV account, not internet specifically.

plans.name: Internet 300

After the promo, Mediacom's standard equipment rates apply (HSI, 2026 rate card: Advanced WiFi 6 $10/mo; WiFi 6 Plus or WiFi 7 $15/mo). There is also a $25 activation fee. The $65 regular price comes from a third party. In upgraded markets such as Des Moines, IA, Mediacom's local page lists 100 Mbps upload.

plans.name: Internet 2 Gig

There is also a $25 activation fee. The $120 regular price comes from HighSpeedInternet.com. In upgraded markets such as Des Moines, IA, upload is up to 1,000 Mbps.

plans.name: Internet 5 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: Upstream usage over 1 TB a month may cut upload speed by up to 50% for the rest of the month.

There is also a $25 activation fee. Upload is 1,000 Mbps per Mediacom's 5 Gig landing page, while WhistleOut listings say 60 Mbps. plans.name: Xtream Connect

HighSpeedInternet.com's Mediacom plans page shows $29.99/mo for 5 years including modem rental and Advanced WiFi 6, while Reviews.org (Jun 2026) says $14.99/mo for qualifying households. The 100/20 Mbps speed comes from Mediacom's 2025 press release (search snippet only). Price and speed are not verified on Mediacom's own site.

isps.name: Nextlink Internet
isps.pricing_basis: Prices on the nextlinkinternet.com product cards (wireless and fiber pages) on 2026-10-27. No autopay discount is mentioned. These exclude taxes, the $3.12/mo Regulatory Recovery Fee and the 0.75% State Cost Recovery Fee (from the broadband labels). Nextlink says 'Some areas may have varied pricing based on current promotions.'

Fiber is in select communities in TX, NE and IA. Fixed wireless runs up to 1 Gbps. A search result (Business Wire via StreetInsider, not read) says Nextlink is deploying Tarana G2 gigabit fixed wireless to 317,000+ locations.

plans.name: Wireless 100
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited. 'Nextlink Internet does not cap data usage or charge overage fees.'
plans.notes: Broadband label NEXT100 (Jan 2026): $50.00, not introductory, no contract, ETF $0. Typical speeds 100/20 Mbps, typical latency 90 ms. Wi-Fi router rental $7/mo. Optional add-ons: extender $7/mo, Next-Fi Whole Home $20/mo, Next-Fi Outdoor $20/mo. The site advertises 'Free Install', which waives the $49.99 standard install fee. A $15 one-time account setup fee still applies per the label. Antenna height problems can need a Personal Mini Tower (from $1,899).

A symmetrical 200/200 variant is listed at the same $60. Latency from the Open Internet statement (<90 ms, all tiers).

plans.notes: The site card shows $90 with no promo footnote and includes an eero Pro 7 router, but broadband label NEXT1000 (Jan 20 2026) and the rate card both say $100.00. Includes an eero 7 router. The rate card lists Fiber Next500 at $55, so area pricing varies. Fiber labels weren't found on the site. The Open Internet statement gives <90 ms for all tiers.

plans.name: Fiber 2 GIG

isps.name: Optimum
isps.pricing_basis: New-customer online prices as advertised on optimum.com/internet and optimum.com/internet/fiber on 2026-10-27, including the $10/mo Auto Pay + Paperless Billing (checking account only) discount. Every advertised price is a 12-month (1 Gig cable: 36-month) auto-renewing rate; afterward the price rises by up to $15/mo per year until unpublished 'standard rates' are reached, so price_monthly (post-promo regular price) is null. Prices and tiers vary by address; fiber and multi-gig are select areas only.
isps.status_notes: Operated by Optimum Communications, Inc. (Altice USA, Inc. renamed itself after its consumer brand in late 2025; Suddenlink markets were rebranded Optimum earlier). The company carries roughly $21B+ of debt with large maturities in 2027 (a ~$4.1B maturity in April 2027 is cited as the key deadline). In June 2026 it moved its eastern footprint into a subsidiary outside existing creditors' reach and raised ~$500M there; in Sep 2026 lenders sued, alleging fraudulent transfers; reports citing the WSJ say a restructuring deal that would hand equity control to lenders (Apollo, Oaktree, JPMorgan among them) is being negotiated, with Chapter 11 possible if talks fail. No filing or signed deal was confirmed as of 2026-10-27. Service is still sold normally.

mobile_bundles.eligible_mobile_plans: Optimum Mobile Unlimited or Unlimited Max
mobile_bundles.notes: 'Optimum Complete' credit of $20/mo on internet (optimum.com/mobile footnote); mobile must be added within 30 days of the internet order. The internet pages show bundle prices of $15 (300 Mbps), $5 (500 Mbps), $25 (1 Gig), $45 (2 Gig), $70 (8 Gig), but some text cites a $10 credit, so the amount is inconsistent across pages. Unlimited lines start at $20/line with 3+ lines, AutoPay required, $25 activation per line. Duration of the credit not stated. Whether Optimum Mobile can be bought without Optimum Internet was not stated on the pages read (the Switch & Save promo requires Optimum Internet).

plans.name: 300 Mbps Fiber
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data; Optimum says speeds on unlimited-data packages may drop during local network congestion.
plans.notes: $35/mo is shown as the list price (no strikethrough). Fine print: auto-renews at $35/mo for 12 months, then up to +$15/mo per year until standard rates. One gateway free ($0/mo for 12 months, then up to +$5/mo per year to an unpublished standard rate). Free self-setup; for online orders 'standard rates for professional installation may apply' (amount not published; third-party sites cite ~$100). With Unlimited/Unlimited Max mobile: $15/mo ($20 credit). Upload speed from the fiber page summary (symmetrical).

plans.name: 500 Mbps Fiber
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data; may slow during local congestion.
plans.notes: Online-only $25/mo shown struck through from a $45/mo list price; both are 12-month rates, then up to +$15/mo per year until standard rates. Gateway $0/mo for 12 months. With Unlimited mobile the page shows $5/mo (inconsistent credit wording: $10 vs $20).

plans.name: 1 Gig Fiber
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data; may slow during local congestion.
plans.notes: Advertised 'up to 940 Mbps' wired. Online-only $45/mo struck from $55/mo list. Fiber page says 12-month term; the main internet page's fine print says $45 for 36 months, so the term may differ by page/address. Up to $50 gift card offered. A 3-year price lock is available by adding the $10/mo Secure WiFi+ add-on (includes HBO Max Basic With Ads). With Unlimited mobile: $25/mo.

plans.name: 2 Gig Fiber
plans.notes: Fine print: '2 Gig Internet service auto-renews monthly at $65/mo. + taxes & fees for 12 months', then up to +$15/mo per year until standard rates. Select fiber areas only. With Unlimited mobile: $45/mo. A third-party tracker citing older Optimum broadband labels listed 2 Gig at $85 rising to $130; not current.

plans.name: 8 Gig Fiber
plans.notes: Fine print: '8 Gig Internet service auto-renews monthly at $90/mo. + taxes & fees for 12 months', then up to +$15/mo per year. 'Not available in all areas.' With Unlimited mobile: $70/mo. No 5 Gig tier was shown on optimum.com today (older third-party listings mention 5 Gig at $115).

plans.name: 300 Mbps
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data; may slow during local congestion.
plans.notes: Hybrid fiber-coax tier (Optimum markets all speeds as 'fiber-powered'); 'up to 300/20 Mbps' per optimum.com/internet. Same price terms as the fiber tier.

plans.name: 500 Mbps
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data; may slow during local congestion.
plans.notes: HFC tier, 'up to 500/20 Mbps'. Online $25/mo struck from $45/mo, 12-month rate.

plans.name: 1 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data; may slow during local congestion.
plans.notes: HFC tier, 'up to 940/35 Mbps'. Fine print on optimum.com/internet: '1 Gig Internet service auto-renews monthly at $45/mo. + taxes & fees for 36 months', then up to +$15/mo per year; the page also labels it '1-year price lock', so price_lock_months is the conservative 12. Shown struck from $55/mo.

isps.name: Quantum Fiber from AT&T
isps.pricing_basis: Fiber: prices from quantumfiber.com and quantumfiber.com/internet.html on 2026-10-27, with the $5/mo AutoPay-from-a-bank-account discount and paperless billing applied. price_monthly = listed monthly recurring charge minus the $5 AutoPay discount; promo_price_monthly = new-customer price after the $25-$30/mo new-customer discount (duration not stated). 2 Gig and 3 Gig offers are 'select markets'. DSL: centurylink.com advertised price with paperless billing.

The site now brands it 'Quantum Fiber from AT&T' (footer: (c) 2026 AT&T Intellectual Property) and still sells under the Quantum Fiber name. Lumen kept the copper network: CenturyLink-branded DSL ('Simply Unlimited Internet') is still advertised on centurylink.com by Lumen, so that plan is included here but is a different operator from the fiber plans.

mobile_bundles.eligible_internet_plans: All Quantum Fiber plans except Simply Fiber
mobile_bundles.eligible_mobile_plans: Eligible AT&T unlimited wireless plan (new customers: min. $60/mo before discounts)
mobile_bundles.notes: $20/mo off the AT&T Wireless bill when you have both services; names and addresses must match; credit appears within 1-3 bill cycles and requires keeping Quantum Fiber. Not available on CenturyLink DSL (different operator).
mobile_bundles.source: https://www.quantumfiber.com/att-offer.html (linked from quantumfiber.com home page; terms read on home page 2026-10-27)

plans.name: 1 Gig
plans.notes: Fine print: 'New Quantum Fiber customers will receive a $25/mo discount off the monthly recurring charge for 940/1-GIG speed ($80mo)' plus $5/mo for bank-account AutoPay; paperless billing required. How long the $25 discount lasts is not stated (promo_months null). If payment method changes or two bank draws fail in 12 months, 'the then-current standard monthly rate will apply'. 360 WiFi (tech decides pod count) included at no added cost. Free technician install; Quantum absorbs the first $1,500 of any construction charge. 'Pricing subject to change' - no price lock stated.

plans.name: 2 Gig

plans.name: 3 Gig
plans.notes: Select markets; appears in fine print rather than as a plan card. Monthly recurring charge $105; new customers get $30/mo off plus $5/mo bank AutoPay = $70. Upload assumed symmetrical per the site's 'all except 2 Gig' statement.

plans.name: Simply Fiber Internet
plans.notes: INCOME-QUALIFIED ONLY: a household member must be in a listed assistance program (SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, etc.), verified via SheerID. 'Limited availability'. 360 WiFi + one pod included; no early termination fee. Not eligible for the AT&T Wireless bundle discount. Upload speed not stated.

plans.name: CenturyLink Simply Unlimited Internet
plans.data_cap_notes: 'CenturyLink offers unlimited data on all internet plans'.
plans.notes: Sold by Lumen under the CenturyLink brand (not AT&T). $55/mo with paperless billing required ($2 per paper bill otherwise), plus taxes and a CTL fee up to $1.50/mo/line; 'Limited time offer', rate 'subject to change'. One price for whatever DSL speed the address can get: the offer card says 'all speeds up to 100 Mbps', another banner says up to 140 Mbps (pair-bonded areas); many addresses get far less. Modem lease up to $17/mo or buy up to $200 + tax, or BYO compatible modem. Self-install up to $25; technician install up to $149; construction charges possible. Month-to-month, no ETF; postpay may need credit check/deposit.

isps.name: Rise Internet (formerly Rise Broadband)
isps.pricing_basis: Prices with the $20/mo AutoPay discount, as shown on the risebroadband.com homepage on 2026-10-27. Without AutoPay, add $20 (shown as the struck-through price). Taxes extra.
isps.status_notes: Rise Broadband rebranded as Rise Internet on Mar 16 2026 and moved its HQ to Dallas/Fort Worth. The site is still risebroadband.com, and its footer reads '(c) 2026 RISE INTERNET'. Rise is a rural fixed-wireless ISP, historically the largest privately held WISP in the US, and also sells fiber in some areas. Owned by GI Partners since 2023 (RCR Wireless). It plans to cover 3.2M more Texas homes and businesses within a year.

isps.name: Sparklight
isps.pricing_basis: Allconnect's 'starting at' prices (updated 2026-10-13) for the main Sparklight lineup. Regular post-promo prices come from HighSpeedInternet.com (Mar 2026) and CompareInternetHub (Sep 21 2026). Promo rates reportedly require autopay + paperless billing. sparklight.com returned HTTP 429 to every fetch today, so nothing was read on the official site. Sparklight runs several legacy and acquired-system lineups (Freedom Connect, Fiber-branded tiers in fiber markets), so names and prices vary by address.
isps.status_notes: Sparklight is the consumer brand of Cable One, Inc. (NYSE: CABO). In Jan 2026, Cable One agreed to buy the remaining 55% of Mega Broadband Investments (MBI, which operates as Vyve Broadband) for about $475-495M plus MBI's net debt. The deal was scheduled to close Oct 1 2026, and a Sep 22 2026 SEC filing shows a $700M revolver draw, but no closing announcement was found as of 2026-10-27. Vyve markets are sold under the Vyve brand and are NOT covered by this file.

mobile_bundles.eligible_internet_plans: Any eligible Sparklight Internet plan (Internet service must stay active for the 12 months)
mobile_bundles.notes: Promo: one free Unlimited line for 12 months for eligible new and existing Sparklight Internet customers. Standard Unlimited pricing ($30/mo) applies afterward, and a SIM activation fee and taxes may apply. Eligibility ends if Internet is cancelled or moved to an ineligible plan. Sparklight Mobile is sold only to Sparklight Internet customers (1GB $15 / 5GB $25 / Unlimited $30). There is no separate ongoing internet discount. The end date was not confirmed today; an earlier pass of this project's sparklight-mobile file read 'offer expires 1/3/27' on the official site.

Equipment is $14.99/mo for modem + eero per Allconnect, while other sources say a modem alone starts at $10.50/mo. In Q1 2026, Sparklight ran a 3-year price-lock campaign (expired 3/31/26).

plans.name: Internet 600
plans.data_cap_notes: No data cap. Accounts using more than 5 TB a month may be slowed during congestion.

Regular prices in other sources range from $70 (CompareInternetHub) to $94 plus a $14.99 lease (HSI). Some areas use 940 Mbps or 'Freedom Connect Gig' naming. A $30 activation fee applies.

The $124 regular price comes from HSI and CompareInternetHub. In fiber markets this tier is 'Fiber 2 Gig' ($74.95-$99 promo reported), with upload likely higher than the 50 Mbps cable figure.

plans.name: Fiber 6 Gig
plans.notes: Sold only in Sparklight's fiber (FTTH) areas. CompareInternetHub (Sep 2026) reports a $99.95-$155 promo and $175 regular. HSI (Mar 2026) lists $115, plus Fiber 300/500/600/1G/2G/3G tiers at $45/$60/$65/$75/$90/$105 in fiber areas. Upload speed is not published, and promo terms are unverified.

plans.name: Sparklight Lift
plans.notes: Low-income program for households that qualify through federal assistance programs (SSI and others). It's a flat $29.95/mo with modem and Wi-Fi included and no contract or credit check (CompareInternetHub, Allconnect).

isps.name: Spectrum
isps.pricing_basis: Online promotional prices for new residential internet-only customers as shown on spectrum.com/internet on 2026-10-27 ('for one year'); 2 Gig and 7 Gig prices from WhistleOut / HighSpeedInternet.com (select markets). Prices vary by address; ordering by phone or in store may cost more.
isps.status_notes: Spectrum is Charter Communications' consumer brand. Charter completed its $34.5B acquisition of Cox Communications (and Liberty Broadband) on Aug 20, 2026; Spectrum products, pricing and packaging rolled out to former Cox markets from mid-September 2026, and cox.com now presents as 'Cox is now Spectrum'. Charter's parent company is to rename itself Cox Communications within a year of closing while keeping the Spectrum consumer brand. Existing legacy Cox customers keep their current Cox products and prices unless they change plans.

Guaranteed.' when you sign up for Spectrum Internet and switch 2+ mobile lines. HighSpeedInternet.com: the internet promo price runs 24 months with Internet + Mobile (36 months with Internet + TV + Mobile) instead of 12. Spectrum One (internet + mobile line + Advanced WiFi) was not described on the pages read. Discount varies by package, so discount_monthly is null.

Modem free; Advanced WiFi router $10/mo (optional, needed for WiFi). installation_fee = $20 activation with self-install; pro install $50 + $20 activation (HighSpeedInternet.com / WhistleOut). MyUtilitySearch says the $40 price is online-only ($50 by phone/store) and estimates ~$75/mo after promo (estimate, not used). Includes Spectrum Mobile free for a year.

plans.name: Internet 1 Gig
plans.notes: Official: $60/mo for one year with Advanced WiFi included, standard rates after (amount not published). Upload 40 Mbps per WhistleOut; HighSpeedInternet.com says Gig upload is up to 500 Mbps in upgraded areas and 35 Mbps elsewhere. MyUtilitySearch estimates ~$95/mo after promo (estimate, not used). Includes Spectrum Mobile free for a year.

plans.name: Internet 2 Gig
plans.notes: Select markets only; spectrum.com shows the tier (with Invincible WiFi included) but no price. $80/mo from WhistleOut and HighSpeedInternet.com; WhistleOut marks it 'not introductory' but whether the price is promotional is unclear, so it is stored as promo with unknown term. MyUtilitySearch lists $70 promo (~$120 after). Symmetrical 2000/2000 per WhistleOut (fiber / high-split markets). Technology may be cable (high-split DOCSIS) or fiber depending on market.

plans.notes: Fiber, select markets only. $140/mo and 7000/7000 Mbps from WhistleOut (marked not introductory) and HighSpeedInternet.com. Not shown on spectrum.com/internet today.

isps.name: Starlink
isps.pricing_basis: US list prices per month before taxes, as reported by SatelliteInternet.com (Oct 6 2026) and KeepTrack (fact-checked Oct 21 2026). No autopay discount exists. starlink.com is a JavaScript app and could not be read on 2026-10-27.
isps.status_notes: SpaceX's low-Earth-orbit satellite service. US Residential was split into speed tiers in Jan 2026: Residential 100 Mbps, Residential 200 Mbps (the renamed Residential Lite) and Residential MAX. All three went up $5-$10 in June 2026, for existing customers too, starting with their June bill.

plans.name: Residential 100 Mbps
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data. The Fair Use Policy can slow the heaviest users when the network is congested, but Starlink publishes no GB threshold. Network priority is lower than on Residential MAX.
plans.notes: Sold only in select areas with spare capacity. The price rose from $50 in June 2026. The Standard Kit costs $349 to buy. In select US areas it is a free rental: $0 upfront plus a reported $20 shipping fee, and the dish must be returned within 30 days of cancelling. A $10/mo kit rental fee was added for new customers in June 2026, and SatelliteInternet.com reported it removed from new residential orders by July 20. In congested cells Starlink adds a one-time demand ('congestion') charge, reported at about $100 to $1,000+ (KeepTrack) or $100 to $1,500 (SatelliteInternet.com); the amount depends on the address. Self-install is standard, and optional professional installation costs up to $199. 30-day money-back trial. Latency: SatelliteInternet.com lists 30-40 ms; 40 ms (the upper bound) is recorded. Starlink publishes no typical speed ranges. Third-party aggregates cite a median of about 92-100+ Mbps down and about 12 Mbps up across all US Starlink users. Spring 2026 promos ($39/mo for 6 months, $29/mo for 3 months, with free hardware) ended Mar 31 and Jun 4.

plans.name: Residential 200 Mbps
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data. Lower network priority than Residential MAX during congestion. Fair Use Policy, with no published GB threshold.
plans.notes: Formerly 'Residential Lite' ($80/mo when it launched in 2025, then capped at 200 Mbps). Sold only in areas with excess bandwidth. The price rose from $80 in June 2026. Kit, free-rental, demand-charge, install and trial terms are the same as on Residential 100 Mbps. Latency 30-40 ms per SatelliteInternet.com (upper bound recorded).

plans.name: Residential MAX
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data with Starlink's highest residential network priority during busy hours.
plans.notes: Marketed as 'up to 400+ Mbps'. Includes a Gen 3 router plus a free Starlink Router Mini as a mesh node (a rental, which must be returned on cancel or downgrade). SatelliteInternet.com says MAX includes free professional home installation. The price rose from $120 in June 2026. Kit purchase is $349, or a free rental in select areas. A demand charge may apply in congested cells. Independent 2026 tests (PCMag reviewer, via search summary) put MAX daily averages at about 145-170 Mbps. A third-party claim of 20-40 Mbps upload could not be confirmed for the US, so upload is null. Latency 30-40 ms per SatelliteInternet.com (upper bound recorded).

isps.name: TDS Telecom
isps.pricing_basis: tdstelecom.com shows plan names and speeds without an address, but prices only after an address check. Prices here are 24-month promo and post-promo figures from CableTV.com's TDS guide (verified 2026-08-05), the most recent priced tracker read. The TDS Connect and TDS Mobile bundle terms were read on tdstelecom.com today. Taxes and fees are extra. In some markets TDS offers 'Price for Life' or 'All-In' (taxes/fees included) pricing instead.
isps.status_notes: TDS Telecom is the wireline unit of Telephone and Data Systems, Inc. Its wireless business, UScellular, was sold to T-Mobile in 2025. TDS has been shedding non-core markets: Texas cable was sold in Nov 2024, Colorado incumbent markets in Jun 2025 and Oklahoma incumbent markets on Dec 31 2025. Remaining footprint at Q2 2026: about 1.2M fiber service addresses (60% of the footprint) plus cable and copper (DSL) markets. TDS also bought Granite State Communications (NH), whose customers are partly served via mygsc.com.

mobile_bundles.eligible_mobile_plans: New TDS Mobile Unlimited and By-the-Gig lines
mobile_bundles.notes: 50% off each new line's TDS Mobile service charges for 12 months, then standard rates. That brings Unlimited to $15/mo per line (standard $29.95, about $15 off) and By-the-Gig to $7/mo (standard $13.95). The discount is lost if TDS Internet is terminated. TDS Mobile is 'only available to TDS broadband internet customers'. There's no ongoing internet-side discount.

plans.name: Extreme300 Fiber Internet
plans.data_cap_notes: TDS fiber is listed as unlimited data.
plans.notes: TDS's page says 'Wi-Fi Included'. The post-promo price is CableTV.com's approximate figure (~$81.95). ISP Reports (TDS FCC label data, Jun 2026) lists a 300M fiber plan at $74.99/mo. Reviewers cite installation fees of $49.95-$99, not confirmed by TDS.

plans.name: Extreme600 Fiber Internet
plans.notes: Listed on TDS's fiber page but not on its main internet-services page, so it may not be sold everywhere. Prices are from CableTV.com (post-promo approximate).

plans.name: 1 Gig Fiber Internet
plans.notes: TDS's page says 'Wi-Fi Included'. CableTV.com: $49.99 promo for 24 months, $89.95 standard, or Price for Life $74.99/mo in some markets. ISP Reports (FCC label data, Jun 2026) shows $74.99.

plans.name: 2 Gig Fiber Internet
plans.notes: Wi-Fi 7 included (TDS page). CableTV.com gives a $69.99-$74.99 promo and a $94.99-$165 post-promo range, so price_monthly is null. ISP Reports (label data) shows $94.99.

plans.name: 5 Gig Fiber Internet
plans.notes: Not shown on TDS's plan pages today; listed by CableTV.com ($99.99 promo, up to $225 after, Price for Life $124.99) and ISP Reports ($124.99). It may be sold only in select markets. The upload figure assumes symmetrical service like other TDS fiber tiers and is unconfirmed.

plans.name: 8 Gig Fiber Internet
plans.notes: TDS lists 8000/8000 Mbps with Wi-Fi 7 included, in select areas. CableTV.com gives a $199.99-$224.99 promo and up to $295 after. ISP Reports shows $224.99.

plans.name: TDS Connect
plans.notes: Low-income plan (TDS site), up to 200 Mbps for $30/mo. For households on Medicaid, SNAP, NSLP, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, or Veterans/Survivors Pension, with annual recertification. Standard Wi-Fi equipment is included and there's no contract. TDS calls it a limited-time offer that isn't available in all areas. Technology depends on the address (technology field set to fiber as a placeholder).

isps.name: T-Mobile Home Internet
isps.pricing_basis: 5G Home: monthly price with AutoPay and no T-Mobile voice line ($50/$60/$70), per WhistleOut and Cord Cutters News (Oct 2026); a qualifying T-Mobile voice line takes $15 off (limited-time $20 off Oct 15 - Dec 2, 2026). Fiber: price with Fiber AutoPay ($10/mo AutoPay discount) per Cord Cutters News (Oct 2026), Slickdeals (Sep 2026) and Reviews.org; 'Pricing based on estimated location; may vary by verified service address.' t-mobile.com returned 403 to automated fetch, so no official page was read. Plus taxes and fees.
isps.status_notes: Covers T-Mobile 5G Home Internet (Rely / Amplified / All-In) and T-Mobile Fiber. T-Mobile Fiber includes the former Metronet footprint (acquired via a joint venture, closed July 2025; Metronet customers are being transitioned to T-Mobile Fiber) and the Lumos joint venture (closed April 2025, Mid-Atlantic). Whether every Lumos market is now sold under the T-Mobile Fiber name was not confirmed.

At the June 2025 fiber launch T-Mobile priced fiber lower with a voice line, but the Oct 2026 fiber offers read (Cord Cutters News, Slickdeals) do not mention a voice-line discount; Reviews.org shows a '2 Gig + voice line' listing at the same $70. Current fiber voice-line discount unknown.

plans.notes: $35/mo with Fiber AutoPay, $45/mo without (Cord Cutters News Oct 2026; Slickdeals Sep 2026; Reviews.org). Reviews.org (in another section) and Android Authority list $45/mo with AutoPay as a new-mover offer, so prices vary by market. Wi-Fi router and installation included (Cord Cutters). Wi-Fi router, mesh extender if needed, and installation included. 5 Gig and higher tiers exist in some former Metronet markets (Reviews.org mentions 5 Gig) but no current price was found.

isps.name: Verizon Home Internet
isps.pricing_basis: 'As low as' prices on verizon.com plan pages read 2026-10-27; Fios prices are 'Discounted pricing with Auto Pay & paper-free billing' without a Verizon mobile plan. With any postpaid Verizon mobile phone plan, Verizon advertises Fios from $30/mo and 5G Home / Lite from $35/mo. Prices vary by address.
