mobile_bundles.eligible_mobile_plans: Any postpaid Verizon mobile phone plan (excludes business and data-only plans)
mobile_bundles.notes: Verizon news release (Jun 16, 2026): home internet customers are 'eligible for a $15/mo discount when they bundle it with the Verizon Simplicity Plan'; home internet starts at $35/mo with a postpaid mobile plan; Auto Pay & paper-free billing required. Mobile + Home customers also get up to $10/mo toward one paid entertainment perk, and the $99 Fios setup fee is waived. The advertised with-mobile entry prices ($30 Fios 300 vs $40 tile; $35 5G Home vs $60 card) imply different gaps than $15, so the effective discount may vary by plan and promo. Verizon also sells a combined plan (home internet + 1 mobile line) at $70/mo after Auto Pay for new customers (verizon.com/mobileandhome).

plans.name: Fios 300 Mbps
plans.data_cap_notes: No data cap stated; Fios is unlimited.
plans.notes: Plan tile: $40/mo with Auto Pay & paper-free, 3-year price guarantee, router included. Verizon headlines 'Plans start at $30/mo for Fios 300 Mbps ... with any Verizon mobile phone plan' (Mobile + Home Discount enrollment required). $99 setup 'may apply unless you are an already existing Verizon mobile customer and enroll in Mobile + Home'. Current promo: '2 Months on Us' bill credit for new eligible plans (limited time, no end date).

plans.name: Fios 500 Mbps
plans.data_cap_notes: No data cap stated; Fios is unlimited.
plans.notes: Plan tile: $75/mo with Auto Pay & paper-free, 3-year price guarantee (HighSpeedInternet.com's Jul 2025 data said 4 years), router included. $99 setup waived with Mobile + Home.

plans.name: Fios 1 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: No data cap stated; Fios is unlimited.
plans.notes: Plan tile: $90/mo with Auto Pay & paper-free; avg wired 750-940 Mbps down / 750-880 up. Price guarantee is shown as 5 years in plan details but 3 years on the plan tile (conflict on Verizon's page; 60 used). Router + Whole-Home Wi-Fi (1 extender). Mobile + Home customers get up to $10/mo toward an eligible perk. $99 setup waived with Mobile + Home.

plans.name: Fios 2 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: No data cap stated; Fios is unlimited.
plans.notes: Plan tile: $100/mo with Auto Pay & paper-free, 5-year price guarantee; avg wired 1.5-2.3 Gbps each way. Router + Whole-Home Wi-Fi (up to 3 extenders). Eligible for Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ perk and Ring bundle promos. Limited availability.

plans.name: Fios 5 Gig
plans.data_cap_notes: No data cap stated; Fios is unlimited.
plans.notes: Plan tile: $110/mo with Auto Pay & paper-free, 5-year price guarantee; avg wired 4.5-5.3 Gbps each way. Router + Whole-Home Wi-Fi Plus. Limited availability.

plans.name: 5G Home
plans.notes: verizon.com/home/internet/5g plan card 'as low as' $60/mo; Verizon advertises 5G Home 'starting at $35/mo' with Auto Pay and any Verizon mobile phone plan. Whether the $60 card already includes Auto Pay is unclear (third-party: MyUtilitySearch Sep 2026 says $50 w/ Auto Pay; BroadbandNow Jul 2026 says $60 w/ Auto Pay). 'Up to 100 Mbps' per Verizon's page article; upload not published. 3-year price lock. Router included; plug-and-play self setup ('Self setup not available in all areas').

plans.name: 5G Home Plus
plans.notes: Plan card 'as low as' $70/mo; 4-year price lock; router included. 'Up to 150 Mbps' per Verizon's page article (reviews.org Apr 2026 gave much higher figures). '$99 professional setup charge may apply. Waived for select plans and locations'; self setup is $0.

plans.name: 5G Home Ultimate
plans.notes: Plan card 'as low as' $85/mo; 5-year price lock; router + 1 Wi-Fi Extender + free router upgrade after 3 years. 'Up to 300 Mbps' per Verizon's page article. '$99 professional setup charge may apply. Waived for select plans and locations'; self setup is $0. Eligible for Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ perk promo.

plans.name: Home Internet Lite
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited, but after 150 GB speeds are lowered to up to 10/3 Mbps (typical 3-10 down / 1-3 up) for the rest of the bill cycle.
plans.notes: Cellular home internet on Verizon's network. Page lists 'as low as' $60/mo (footnote 'Discounted pricing with Auto Pay & any Verizon mobile phone plan') while the headline says 'Starting at $35/mo' with Auto Pay + any Verizon mobile plan; at Oct 2025 launch 9to5Mac reported $50 with Auto Pay / $60 without. Exact basis of the $60 is unclear. 3-year price lock; router included.

plans.name: Home Internet Lite Extra
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited, but after 200 GB speeds are lowered to up to 10/3 Mbps for the rest of the bill cycle.
plans.notes: Page lists 'as low as' $80/mo; HighSpeedInternet.com (Jul 2025 data) gave $80 with Auto Pay and $55 with a postpaid Verizon mobile plan. 4-year price lock; router + 1 Wi-Fi Extender + router upgrade after 3 years; optional Whole-Home Wi-Fi Plus $5/mo.

isps.name: Viasat
isps.pricing_basis: Monthly service prices on viasat.com/home-internet/plans and fiber.viasat.com on 2026-10-27. These exclude the $15/mo satellite equipment lease, taxes and a monthly Administrative Cost Recovery Fee ($1.23-$3.49; Viasat's label contradicts itself). Viasat's legal terms say plans and terms vary by location.
isps.status_notes: Geostationary satellite ISP, available nationwide wherever there is a clear view of the southern sky. Since 2026 Viasat also sells Viasat Fiber in a few California cities (Escondido, Placentia, Simi Valley).

plans.name: Essentials
plans.data_cap_notes: 150 GB of High-Speed Data per month, then unlimited 'Standard Data' that Viasat may put behind other customers during congestion (slower). No hard cap or overage fee.
plans.notes: Viasat lists 'up to 80 Mbps most of the time' baseline and bursts up to 150 Mbps; download_mbps = burst. The promo is for new customers only, for 12 months. Free standard installation ('a $335 value'), but a one-time activation fee may be charged (amount not published). Alternatively, a $250 one-time 'Lifetime Lease' replaces the $15/mo lease. Contract: Viasat says plans are either no-contract or 24-month depending on plan and location, and doesn't say which applies to Essentials. WhistleOut lists Essentials as a 24-month term with an ETF of $15 per remaining month, so contract_months is null. WhistleOut (from the broadband label): typical 36 Mbps down / 5 Mbps up, latency 601 ms, max upload 5 Mbps.

plans.name: Unleashed
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited High-Speed Data. Users trending above 'typical usage' (what 70% of residential customers use; the broadband label puts it at 850 GB in any 30 days) may get reduced priority during congestion.
plans.notes: Baseline 'up to 80 Mbps most of the time', bursts up to 180 Mbps; download_mbps = burst. The plan card says 'No data caps or contracts' (month-to-month, no ETF). Free standard installation, though an activation fee may be charged. WhistleOut's label-derived figures (typical 28 Mbps down / 9 Mbps up, 616 ms) look inconsistent, so typical ranges are left null. Office Hours is not available on Unleashed.

plans.name: Unleashed Max
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited High-Speed Data with 'Priority Network': priority over other Viasat customers. The same typical-usage deprioritization policy as Unleashed applies.
plans.notes: New ('ALL-NEW!') in 2026. Baseline 'up to 80 Mbps most of the time', bursts up to 200 Mbps. The plan card shows a struck-through '$99.99/mo' with '$70 off', which conflicts with the FAQ and footnote ($109.99 for 12 months, then $179.99). The FAQ/footnote figure is recorded. WhistleOut (label-derived): typical 200 Mbps down / 3 Mbps up, 616 ms.

plans.name: Viasat Fiber 500 Mbps
plans.notes: Sold only in select California cities (Escondido, Placentia, Simi Valley per fiber.viasat.com). Month-to-month with no ETF. Free professional installation, but a one-time activation fee is charged (amount not published). The ONT doubles as the router, and the page names no equipment fee. 'First month free' applies on unspecified 'select plans', so no promo is recorded. The page also shows a generic 'starting at $99.99/mo' string that conflicts with the per-plan prices, and the per-plan price is recorded.

plans.name: Viasat Fiber 1 GIG
plans.notes: California fiber footprint only. Terms are the same as Viasat Fiber 500 Mbps. Moving to a slower Viasat Fiber plan costs a $30 transition fee (Viasat Fiber FAQ, via search summary).

plans.name: Viasat Fiber 2 GIG
plans.notes: California fiber footprint only. Terms are the same as Viasat Fiber 500 Mbps.

plans.name: Viasat Fiber 5 GIG
plans.notes: California fiber footprint only. Terms are the same as Viasat Fiber 500 Mbps. Only $10 more than 2 GIG as listed on 2026-10-27.

plans.name: Viasat FiberAid 1 GIG
plans.notes: Low-income plan for 'qualifying households' only (criteria not published). California fiber footprint only.

isps.name: WOW! Internet
isps.pricing_basis: price_monthly is the Monthly Price on WOW!'s own FCC Broadband Facts labels, read 2026-10-27. Labels show it as non-introductory, without AutoPay and with paperless billing (paper statements add $4/mo). WOW! says the price does not rise automatically after 12/24 months. Advertised AutoPay prices are lower (Reviews.org Apr 2026: $30/$45/$60 for 300/600/1 Gig, i.e. $10 below label), but WOW!'s AutoPay discount 'may vary depending upon your service plan', so it is not applied here. Taxes are extra. Prices and tiers vary by market.
isps.status_notes: WideOpenWest, Inc. was taken private by DigitalBridge and Crestview Partners funds in a deal of about $1.5B EV ($5.20/share). The closing was announced Dec 31 2025, and the shares were delisted. WOW! still operates under its own brand.

mobile_bundles.notes: WOW! says 'Save up to $10 off your mobile bill when bundled with WOW! Internet', with mobile from $15/mo per line when bundled. This project's wow-mobile research (2026-10-25, from WOW!'s Reach storefront plan data) found $10 off the first line and $5 off each added line on the shared-data plans, and $10 off per line on All-in Unlimited. That research also found standalone (no-internet) prices in the plan data, so internet appears optional, but that was not confirmed on wowway.com today. Service is provided by That's My Mobile (Reach platform).

plans.name: Internet 300
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data; label shows no additional data charges.
plans.notes: Label typical speeds are 350 Mbps down / 20 Mbps up, so upload_mbps is the label's typical figure, not an advertised max. Professional install is $99; self-install activation is $10. A WiFi modem is included, or you can bring your own (no discount). Optional Price Lock for Life is about $5/mo extra. Advertised with AutoPay at $30/mo (Reviews.org) or $25/mo (myutilitysearch, Oct 2026).

plans.name: Internet 600
plans.notes: Label typical speeds are 650 Mbps down / 47 Mbps up, so upload_mbps is the label's typical figure. Self-install activation is $10. Advertised with AutoPay at $45/mo (Reviews.org Apr 2026) or $35/mo (myutilitysearch Oct 2026). Price Lock for Life is about $5/mo extra.

plans.name: Internet 1 Gig
plans.notes: Label typical speeds are 1,093 Mbps down / 43 Mbps up, so upload_mbps is the label's typical figure. Self-install activation is $10. Advertised with AutoPay at $60/mo (Reviews.org) or $50/mo (myutilitysearch, ISP Reports). Price Lock for Life is about $5/mo extra.

plans.name: Fiber 1 Gig (Internet 1 Gig Symmetrical Price Lock)
plans.notes: Official label 'Internet 1 Gig Symmetrical Price Lock' shows $80/mo, non-introductory, typical 941/936 Mbps, 5 ms latency. The name includes a price lock, but the label gives no lock length, so price_lock_months is null (WOW!'s lock product is 'Price Lock for Life'). A WOW!-supplied ONT is required in fiber areas. Reviews.org lists Fiber 1 Gig at $80 with AutoPay. ISP Reports shows a $50 promo vs $80 regular.

isps.name: Xfinity
isps.pricing_basis: Promo / price-guarantee prices with Autopay (stored bank account) + paperless billing, as advertised nationally on xfinity.com/national on 2026-10-27 for 300 Mbps and Gig; 500 Mbps and 2 Gig from CableTV.com (pricing verified 7/21/26). Xfinity prices by address; taxes and fees extra.
isps.status_notes: Xfinity is Comcast's consumer brand. NOW Internet is Comcast's prepaid internet brand, sold through xfinity.com/now.

mobile_bundles.eligible_internet_plans: Any Xfinity Internet plan (the free Mobile Select line needs residential post-paid 300 Mbps or above)
mobile_bundles.eligible_mobile_plans: Mobile Select ($30/mo with internet) and Mobile Plus ($45/mo with internet), per line
mobile_bundles.notes: Official: 'Xfinity Mobile is exclusively available to Xfinity Internet members'; advertised mobile prices 'include $10/mo internet customer discount'. Promos for new mobile customers: 1 free Mobile Select line for the first year (12 monthly bill credits; requires residential post-pay 300 Mbps+ internet), or Mobile Plus at $15/mo for the first year then $45/mo. No discount on the internet bill itself was found.

plans.name: 300 Mbps (1-Year Price)
plans.notes: Official page: '$40/mo ... Get our lowest price for one year. WiFi equipment and unlimited data included.' Offer ends 12/1, new Xfinity Internet customers only. Price after year 1 not shown on the page; Comcast's June 2025 lineup set a $70/mo 'everyday' price for 300 Mbps, but that figure is >1 year old and not re-verified. Upload 100 Mbps is from CableTV.com (third-party); Xfinity upload speeds vary by market.

plans.name: 300 Mbps (5-Year Price Guarantee)
plans.notes: Official page: '$45/mo for 5 years ... Includes unlimited data, WiFi equipment, same-day setup, and our 5-Year Price Guarantee. No contract, cancel anytime.' Price after 5 years not shown officially; CableTV.com says '+$30.00/mo' after 5 years (third-party). Upload 100 Mbps per CableTV.com. Eligible for 1 free Xfinity Mobile Select line for a year (300 Mbps+).

plans.name: 500 Mbps (5-Year Price Guarantee)
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data included on current national plans.
plans.notes: Not shown on xfinity.com/national today; price and speeds from CableTV.com (pricing verified 7/21/26, includes $10/mo autopay + paperless discount, '+$30.00/mo' after 5 years). Medium confidence.

plans.name: Gig (5-Year Price Guarantee)
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data included on current national plans.
plans.notes: Official page lists 'Gig WiFi built for streaming' at $60/mo for 5 years. CableTV.com (verified 7/21/26) shows 1 Gig at $70/mo for 5 years, so the official $60 appears to be the current offer. Upload 100 Mbps per CableTV.com. Price after 5 years not shown officially.

plans.name: 2 Gig (5-Year Price Guarantee)
plans.data_cap_notes: Unlimited data included on current national plans.
plans.notes: Not shown on xfinity.com/national today; price and 250 Mbps upload from CableTV.com (verified 7/21/26). Not available in all areas.

plans.name: NOW Internet 100 Mbps (prepaid)
plans.notes: Prepaid, paid monthly. Official xfinity.com/now: 'Internet starting at $30/mo' and 'The price you see is the price you get'. Speeds per CableTV.com (Jan 2026). Whether equipment is included is unclear (CableTV.com contradicts itself). Not available in all areas.

plans.name: NOW Internet 200 Mbps (prepaid)
plans.notes: Prepaid. Price and speeds from CableTV.com (Jan 8, 2026); not confirmed on xfinity.com/now today. Not available in all areas.

isps.name: Ziply Fiber
isps.pricing_basis: Ziply's site lists the tiers but only shows prices after an address is entered ('as low as $35/month' headline). Prices recorded are third-party with paperless billing + autopay (debit/ACH) discount: Reviews.org (2026-06-25) intro and post-promo prices, cross-checked against WhistleOut (undated, read 2026-10-27) and FCC-label records aggregated by InternetProviders.ai (undated). Intro prices last 12 months per Reviews.org. Prices vary by market.
isps.status_notes: Owned by BCE Inc. (Bell Canada parent) since its acquisition of Ziply closed in Aug 2025; still sold under the Ziply Fiber brand (Ziply is a trademark of Northwest Fiber, LLC). Footprint: Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana (former Frontier Northwest). Sells fiber 100 Mbps-50 Gig plus legacy DSL to new customers.

plans.name: Fiber 100/100
plans.data_cap_notes: Ziply: 'No data caps or annual contracts.'
plans.notes: $35 matches Ziply's 'as low as $35/month' headline and WhistleOut; $75 post-promo from Reviews.org. Unlike higher tiers, Ziply's fine print does not say a router is included (Reviews.org fee table, data as of 2024, lists an optional $12/mo router lease). Free professional installation when required ($90 value) through 2026-10-28 promo; $90 recorded as the standard fee. Typical speed 103/103 and 4 ms latency from FCC-label data (WhistleOut / InternetProviders.ai).

plans.name: Fiber 300/300
plans.notes: SUSPECT PRICE: Reviews.org lists $80 intro / $95 after, which is more than its Fiber Gig intro ($65); FCC-label aggregations show a 300 Mbps tier at $40. Verify before display. Wi-Fi 7 router included (official fine print). Free pro install when required through 2026-10-28.

plans.name: Fiber Gig
plans.notes: Reviews.org: $65 intro (12 mo) then $115. WhistleOut shows $60; FCC-label aggregation shows $60. Wi-Fi 7 router included (official). Typical speeds from WhistleOut label data.

plans.name: 2 Gig Fiber
plans.notes: Reviews.org: $80 intro then $120. WhistleOut shows $75; label aggregations show $70-$90. Official promo: first month free in select areas through 2026-10-28. Wi-Fi 7 router included.

plans.name: 5 Gig Fiber
plans.notes: Reviews.org: $90 intro then $130 (label aggregation shows $80-$100). Wi-Fi 7 router included; free pro install when required ($90 value) and first month free in select areas through 2026-10-28.

plans.name: 10 Gig Fiber
plans.notes: Official: 'Professional installation for $300'; requires 10 Gig-capable equipment, wiring and devices; static IPv4/IPv6 included. $300/mo price from FCC-label records (InternetProviders.ai, undated); not shown on ziplyfiber.com without an address.

plans.name: 50 Gig Fiber
plans.notes: Official: 'Professional installation for $600'; customer must supply a router with a QSFP28 port (Ziply recommends a MikroTik CCR2216-1G-12XS-2XQ), so equipment_upfront is the cost of that router (not set). $900/mo from FCC-label records (InternetProviders.ai, undated) and Reviews.org's top-of-range figure.

plans.name: DSL Internet
plans.notes: Official: DSL 'For new residential customers only', 'Professional installation for $90'. Price/speed third-party: Reviews.org $50/mo, up to 115 Mbps (most addresses far less); FCC-label records mostly show $55/mo for DSL at 6-134 Mbps. Equipment fee unknown.
